title: publish() metrics callback lets KeyError/ValueError escape into the execution memory-pressure hot path and abort a live job
description: The `publish` closure installed as `ExecutionContext.memory_pressure_callback` wraps ONLY `store.require_job(job_id)` in `try/except Exception: return`. The two operations that run after the guard — `require_job_status(job)` (raises `ValueError` on a status not in `JOB_STATUSES`) and `store.atomic_update(job_id, {...}, expected_status=RUNNING_STATUS)` (raises `KeyError` when `job_id` is no longer present) — are OUTSIDE the try/except. `memory_pressure_callback(event)` is invoked unguarded from `ExecutionContext._record_memory_pressure_events` (`_execution_context.py:947-948`), which runs on the execution sampling path via `_observe_rss`. The `stage()` contextmanager only catches `ExecutionMemoryLimitExceededError`, so a `KeyError`/`ValueError` raised here propagates up and aborts the running execution. The reachable trigger is a TOCTOU eviction/deletion: `require_job` succeeds, then the running job is evicted by TTL (`_evict_stale` for a stale running job, see `_job_store.py:106-111`) or removed via `delete_job`/`clear_result_data` on another thread, then `atomic_update` does `old = self._jobs[job_id]` (`_job_store.py:413`, documented `Raises KeyError if job_id does not exist`) and raises `KeyError`. A best-effort metrics publish thereby becomes a fatal execution failure. The `if status != RUNNING_STATUS: return` guard does not help because it runs before the window and does not prevent eviction of a running job.
evidence:
_job_lifecycle.py: `try:
    job = store.require_job(job_id)
except Exception:
    return
status = require_job_status(job)  # ValueError escapes here
if status != RUNNING_STATUS:
    return
store.atomic_update(job_id, {...}, expected_status=RUNNING_STATUS)  # KeyError escapes if job evicted`. Callback invoked unguarded at _execution_context.py:947-948 `if self.memory_pressure_callback is not None: self.memory_pressure_callback(event)`, reached from _observe_rss -> _record_memory_pressure_events; stage() at _execution_context.py:726-728 only catches ExecutionMemoryLimitExceededError. atomic_update raises KeyError per _job_store.py:413 and its docstring.
